recognize_zh: 周邊血液中的分葉核嗜中性球，細胞質內布滿粗大深紫色的毒性顆粒（toxic granulation），右上方還有一小片淡藍色的 Döhle body，符合 G-CSF 刺激後的變化。
features: Segmented neutrophil with three to four lobes and clumped chromatin
Prominent coarse dark purple (toxic) granules throughout the cytoplasm
Small pale blue cytoplasmic patch near the periphery consistent with a Döhle body
Surrounding red cells are normocytic and normochromic with central pallor
No cytoplasmic vacuoles or organisms identified in this cell
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mature segmented neutrophil with coarse, dark purple cytoplasmic granulation throughout the cytoplasm and a small peripheral pale blue inclusion consistent with a Döhle body. The nucleus shows normal segmentation and chromatin condensation. Background red cells are unremarkable. In the setting of growth factor therapy, these findings are consistent with G-CSF effect; the same toxic changes are also seen in infection and inflammation.

ddx.vs: Morphologically identical toxic granulation and Döhle bodies, so the distinction rests on history of G-CSF administration versus clinical evidence of infection.
Shows large dark azurophilic granules in all leukocytes including lymphocytes and monocytes, persistent in health and not accompanied by Döhle bodies.
Has larger, more sharply defined spindle-shaped blue inclusions with giant platelets and thrombocytopenia, without toxic granulation.
